body.statement: For every prespecified \(\delta\in[0,1]\), if \(\mathcal P_\delta(b,q,\omega)\neq\varnothing\), the extended set in \(\text{def:extended-ratio-image}\) is exactly the set of vaccine challenge-risk ratios compatible with \(\mathfrak M_\delta(b,q,\omega)\). The finite positive-denominator values, the \(+\infty\) branch when \(\rho_{21}=0<\rho_{11}\), and the full \([0,+\infty]\) branch when \(\rho_{11}=\rho_{21}=0\) each have a compatible full-law certificate.
body.justification: The causal identified set remains mathematically defined when no uniform lower bound on the vaccine reference risk is imposed.
body.gap: Janvin and Stensrud (2025) analyze finite single-pathogen ratios; the extended zero-denominator fibers created by changing variants and external margins are not covered by their endpoint formula.
body.consumer: Analysts can report a valid sharp set, including infinite or completely unidentified branches, rather than silently deleting compatible zero-risk laws.
